assessments.reasoning: The first two lines of the digest-matched release LICENSE join SQLiteStudio, GNU GPL version 3 and the following special exception in one sentence. The following GPL heading identifies Version 3, 29 June 2007. Inspection through byte 35891 places the later-version sample in instructions for authors of new programs.

In its assigned context role, the pinned SPDX record identifies the particular following exception and reproduces its GNU GPL observance clause. Its text is consistent with the project's opening. It leaves the base version unspecified, so the version finding depends on the publisher.

The project ref names exactly 3.4.21 and directly targets e42e5688d8e5e6cd79cf745291288863ba74c192. Matching that target to the raw LICENSE commit binds the numbered-base declaration to the claimed edition.

challenge.method: Tested a GPL-3.0-or-later reading against the project opening, GPL section 14 and the closing “How to Apply These Terms to Your New Programs” example. Also checked whether the SPDX exception text identifies the numbered base independently.
challenge.results: Section 14 conditions a later-version choice on the applicable program notice. The closing example uses placeholders for the program and author and illustrates an “any later version” notice after the end of the terms. The actual SQLiteStudio opening explicitly names version 3 and contains no later-version election. SPDX's exception text names the GNU GPL without a version number. The publisher opening therefore decides the narrow base claim.

limitations: The opening alone cannot resolve a later-version election for an individual file or establish an exclusive version choice across the project. The opaque target is understood in the supplied GPL-3.0 scope.
The relationship records what this publisher representation says. Applicability to particular files, distributions or other exceptions requires its own evidence.
reasoning: The release LICENSE begins “SQLiteStudio is licensed under the GNU General Public License version 3 with the addition of the following special exception”. The next paragraph grants the OpenSSL linking permission for portions of the program. This expressly identifies the documented base as GNU GPL version 3. The claim's GPL-3.0 scope is supported at that level of specificity.
